title: Joint conservativity of pro-etale restriction for condensed coefficient complexes
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\{u_i:U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be a pro-etale covering family of $X$ in $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. With $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and $D(T,\Lambda)=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_T)$ the ordinary unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let $u_i^*=Lu_i^*:D(X,\Lambda)\to D(U_i,\Lambda)$ be the derived module inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] for the coefficient identification $\alpha_{u_i}:u_i^{-1}\Lambda_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{U_i}$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]; under the identification $(U_i)_{\mathrm{proet}}\simeq X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U_i$ of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] and $u_i^{-1}G\cong G|_{U_i}$ of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] it is restriction $K\mapsto K|_{U_i}$. Then the functors $u_i^*$ are jointly conservative: a morphism in $D(X,\Lambda)$ is an isomorphism if and only if each $u_i^*$ carries it to an isomorphism. Equivalently, $K|_{U_i}=0$ for all $i$ implies $K=0$.

source.place: Lemma 4.5 proof: restriction to a w-contractible affine cover is conservative; the sheaf descent argument gives the stated covering-family form

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $\mathcal O=\Lambda_X$. For each $i$, clause (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $(U_i)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $\mathcal C/U_i$. Clause 1 of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] identifies $u_i^{-1}G$ naturally with $G|_{U_i}$ for every abelian sheaf and every ring sheaf $G$. In particular, compose $u_i^{-1}\mathcal O\cong\mathcal O|_{U_i}$ with the ring isomorphism $\alpha_{u_i}$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] to identify $\mathcal O|_{U_i}$ with $\Lambda_{U_i}$. By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], the module inverse image is exact, and extension along this ring isomorphism just transports the action: $m\otimes r\mapsto\alpha_{u_i}^{-1}(r)m$ has inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Thus $u_i^*$ on module sheaves is exact slice restriction with this coefficient identification, and $Lu_i^*$ is its termwise functor on the unbounded derived categories. The constant-ring clauses of the localization and inverse-image lemmas are not used.

source.place: Section 3, paragraph beginning If f:Y -> X is any morphism of schemes; Lemma 4.5 proof, the functor j*

proof.text: For every object $V\to X$ of $\mathcal C$, clause 1 of [det-pe-topos-functoriality-site] says that $\{V\times_X U_i\to V\}_i$ is a covering. Each domain admits its projection to $U_i$. Therefore the sieve of arrows $W\to V$ whose domain admits a morphism to some $U_i$ contains a covering family and is a covering sieve. This is exactly the covering hypothesis in [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism]. The site and index family are taken in the common universe of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], so this is a small-site application.

source.place: Lemma 4.5 proof, conservativity; base change of the covering to every site object

proof.text: Let $a:M\to N$ be a morphism of $\mathcal O$-module sheaves whose restrictions to all $U_i$ are isomorphisms. Forget the actions and apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] with value category abelian groups and the covering condition of Step 2. It gives an inverse $b:N\to M$ of the underlying abelian-sheaf map. This inverse is $\mathcal O$-linear: for every object $V$, $r\in\mathcal O(V)$ and $y\in N(V)$, $a_V(b_V(ry))=ry=a_V(r b_V(y))$, so injectivity of $a_V$ gives $b_V(ry)=r b_V(y)$. By the definition of module morphisms in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $b$ is a module morphism and $a$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps; cover-local isomorphism criterion as stated by lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism

proof.text: Write $r_i$ for the exact module restriction of Step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to obtain $H^n(r_i C)\cong r_i H^n(C)$ naturally in every cochain complex $C$, for every integer $n$. These isomorphisms descend to the derived categories: cohomology and termwise exact restriction invert quasi-isomorphisms, and the two composites are the factorizations through the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Naturality holds for images of chain maps by the cited lemma; it also holds for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms by inverting the same naturality square, hence for their composites, which generate the localization. Consequently, for any derived morphism $f:K\to L$, the map $H^n(u_i^*f)$ is identified with $r_i(H^n(f))$.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor; degreewise homology comparison, followed by the defining localization of the derived category

proof.text: Suppose every $u_i^*f$ is invertible. For every integer $n$, its cohomology $H^n(u_i^*f)$ is invertible, since cohomology is a functor. Step 4 then says that all restrictions $r_i(H^n(f))$ are invertible. Apply Step 3 to the module-sheaf morphism $H^n(f)$: it is invertible for every $n$. The unbounded criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], applied to the abelian category of $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves, now gives that $f$ is invertible. Conversely every functor $u_i^*$ preserves inverses, so invertibility of $f$ implies invertibility of all $u_i^*f$.

source.place: Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic; the equivalent cohomology criterion of DerivedCategory.isIso_iff

proof.text: If $K|_{U_i}=0$ for every $i$, apply Step 5 to the unique morphism $K\to0$. Exact additive restriction preserves the zero object, so every restriction of this morphism is an isomorphism between zero objects. Hence $K\to0$ is an isomorphism and $K=0$. This argument includes the empty cover of the empty scheme: Step 2 still supplies a covering sieve at every object, and the sheaf condition forces the only section group on the empty object to be zero. No boundedness of complexes or quasi-compactness of $X$ was assumed.

source.place: Lemma 4.5 proof, conservativity, expressed as detection of zero objects

proof_origin.place: Section 3 and Lemma 4.5 proof; explicit arbitrary-cover cohomology argument using Stacks 04TQ, 010N and 05RT

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N1-9373feb6c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item: statement, six steps, every cited node's statement and the parent's citing step. Source: HRS 2305.18131 §3 (Λ_X=p_X^{-1}Λ; f^* exact) and the Lemma 4.5 proof, which asserts j^* is conservative for a w-contractible affine cover. The item's statement for arbitrary covering families, with the actual condensed coefficients, is true and stronger than that sentence, and the split proves it. Step 1: clause (1) of the localization lemma, clause 1 of the inverse-image restriction lemma (which holds for any ring sheaf), the ring isomorphism α (sfb Lan pullback, whose pointwise formula is the colimit over I_U in def-weil-proetale-inverse-image), and the exactness and scalar transport of def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations. No constant-ring clause is used. Step 2: clause 1 of det-pe-topos-functoriality-site gives the base-changed covering, which is the CoversTop hypothesis of Sheaf.isIso_of_coversTop (I read LocalProperties.lean:35). Step 3: the cancellation proving the inverse linear is correct. Step 4: the exact-functor cohomology isomorphism is natural in chain maps and descends through the localization Q (Q(s) and Q(s)^{-1} generate it). Step 5: DerivedCategory.isIso_iff covers all n and the unbounded category. Step 6 is elementary. Edge cases: empty X, empty family on nonempty X (not a covering), infinite families, Λ=0, unbounded complexes. No duplicate in the DAG or blueprint: the étale cover-detects-iso, Noetherian stratum detection, w-contractible sections and finite stalk-conservative nodes all differ. I accept both declared tool_uses (lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction and det-pe-topos-functoriality-site) as generic site infrastructure. No SGA is cited. No changes were made.

lean.statement: theorem condensed_cover_restriction_conservative (Λ : Profinite.CondensedRing.{u}) [IsCommMonObj Λ.X] (X : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : Scheme.Cover.{v} Scheme.proetalePrecoverage X) : (∀ (K L : DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ.X X))) (f : K ⟶ L), IsIso f ↔ ∀ i : 𝒰.I₀, IsIso ((CondensedRing.upperStar Λ.X (𝒰.f i)).mapDerivedCategory.map f)) ∧ (∀ K : DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ.X X)), (∀ i : 𝒰.I₀, IsZero ((CondensedRing.upperStar Λ.X (𝒰.f i)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)) → IsZero K)
